title: Touring the F5 BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes Lab to Make AI Clusters More Efficient
gist: Sponsored tour of F5's lab showing BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes running on NVIDIA BlueField-3 DPUs to handle LLM routing, token governance and L4-L7 security, freeing host CPUs and aiming to raise GPU efficiency. The supplied text is truncated before any performance results.

insights.claim: F5 BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes (BNK) runs the BIG-IP application delivery and security stack on NVIDIA BlueField-3 DPUs, and can alternatively run on host CPUs, where it consumes valuable cores.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: DPU offload preserves host CPU cores in AI clusters, supporting demand for BlueField DPUs.
insights.quote: It can also run on host CPUs, but then it consumes those valuable cores.

insights.claim: F5 BNK sits between clients and GPU infrastructure to handle LLM routing, token governance, and L4 to L7 security at the network edge.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Inference traffic management is becoming a distinct software layer in AI infrastructure; watch F5's AI-related positioning.

insights.claim: The author says BNK brings much of what used to live on F5 hardware appliances onto BlueField-3 DPUs, indicating a shift of appliance functions toward DPUs.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Appliance-to-DPU migration could reshape how networking and security vendors deliver products.

insights.claim: Raising GPU performance meaningfully through network-edge offload yields more performance from the same power and GPU footprint, which the author names as constraints today.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Efficiency tools that lift utilization are valuable while power and GPU supply bind.
insights.quote: If you can find ways to increase GPU performance in a meaningful way, that means you can get more performance from the same power and GPU footprint, both constraints today.

insights.claim: AI clusters contain many separate networks: GPU-to-GPU, GPU-to-storage, user and application, node and host OS control planes, switches, cooling, PDUs and serial consoles, so networking is far from easy.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Management and application-delivery complexity creates room for software and DPU vendors.

insights.claim: High-speed AI cluster networks often run at 400Gbps or 800Gbps per port.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Port speeds set the bar for switch, NIC and DPU demand.

insights.claim: The F5 test cluster used Supermicro servers with NVIDIA H100 GPUs, with each GPU server holding two BlueField-3 DPUs and top 2U servers holding eight DPUs each; the DPUs have their own management interfaces.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: DPU counts per server show DPUs as a growing component of GPU cluster bills of materials.

insights.claim: The F5 lab tour was sponsored by F5, and STH invested in Keysight IxNetwork and CyPerf load generators each capable of over 1.6Tbps of traffic.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Treat the vendor-favorable framing as sponsored; the article is truncated before the performance results.
insights.quote: we have to say this is sponsored by F5
